about.title: Personal Injury Help in Coalinga, California
about.longDescription: Coalinga sits along Rt 33, with Forest Avenue, E Polk Street, and E Elm Avenue carrying much of the town's daily traffic. In the most recent full year on record, Coalinga saw 11 injury collisions and 15 people hurt, with no traffic deaths reported. Those numbers reflect a small city, but any one of those collisions can turn a normal week into a stack of medical bills, missed work, and confusing paperwork. LawProactive is a free connection service — not a law firm. We don't practice law, charge fees, or handle your case directly. What we do is listen to what happened, then connect you with an independent personal injury attorney in our network who can evaluate your situation and explain your options. Those attorneys work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. If you were injured on Coalinga's roads, at work, or somewhere else in Fresno County, reaching out costs nothing and there's no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity was involved. Waiting too long can close the door on a claim entirely.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't End Your Case
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: California places no limit on non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in typical personal injury cases. That means your claim isn't artificially capped before you even start.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they win or settle your case. That structure lets you get legal help without adding financial pressure to an already hard time.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent personal injury attorneys in Fresno County and elsewhere. We don't provide legal advice or represent you directly — the attorney you're connected with handles your case.

items.question: How much does it cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. Connecting with an attorney through us is free, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if they recover money for you. There's no upfront cost or obligation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury claim in California. If a government agency is involved, that window can be as short as six months, so it's worth acting sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Coalinga?
items.answer: Public collision records show that Rt 33, Forest Avenue, E Polk Street, and E Elm Avenue are among the higher-volume corridors for reported injury crashes in Coalinga. Reports also tend to cluster on Thursdays between roughly 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply record counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, so being partly at fault doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your final recovery would just be reduced by your percentage of fault, which an attorney can help sort out.
